subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow core `read` fallback for known PDF/Office binary document formats now, or defer this issue to broader document parsing/provider-native file architecture?
rationale: Current source still has the token-waste behavior, but the issue explicitly offers fallback versus parsing paths and related open issues cover larger document ingestion/security/ownership decisions.

options.title: Land Narrow Read Fallback
options.body: Guard known binary document reads in the core read-tool path and return a clear message while preserving existing text and image behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Document Architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open as context for provider-native file/document extraction work and avoid a one-off read-tool guard until that architecture is chosen.

options.title: Reject Core Handling
options.body: Decide that document parsing/avoidance belongs entirely in plugins or user tools, then document the supported alternative before closing this issue.

recommendation.title: Land Narrow Read Fallback
recommendation.body: Guard known binary document reads in the core read-tool path and return a clear message while preserving existing text and image behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current read-tool source history points here, and the decision crosses agent runtime behavior and safe defaults.
